findings.title: Food properly labeled; original container.
findings.comment: It was observed that there is not any allergen labeling on items throughout the breakfast buffet. According to the 2022 FDA Food Code, there needs to be allergen labeling on all buffet food items or bulk food items that are available for consumer self-service. Every food item on the buffet is labeled with the name of the food. If the allergen is not in the name of the food, the allergen needs to be listed for consumers to be aware of. This can be accomplished through a poster, on each individual item or display case, or as a QR code. Ensure that all buffet foods are labeled with the major allergens they contain by next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 3-602.11(C) Food Labels. (C) Bulk FOOD that is available for CONSUMER self-dispensing shall be prominently labeled with the following information in plain view of the CONSUMER: (1) The manufacturer's or processor's label that was provided with the FOOD; or (2) A card, sign, or other method of notification that includes the information specified under Subparagraphs (B)(1), (2), (5) and (6) of this section.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: The handwashing sink in the kitchen was observed to not have any paper towels at it at the start of the inspection. CORRECTED- An employee replaced the paper towels. Ensure that each handwashing sink always has a supply of individual, disposable towels to allow for the proper use of a barrier during handwashing.
findings.citation_text: 6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels.

findings.title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
findings.comment: REPEAT- There are bowls in the buffet area that are observed to have the food contact surface exposed to contamination. Ensure that these bowls are inverted or covered to protect the food- and lip-contact surfaces from contamination.
findings.citation_text: 4-904.11(A) Kitchenware and Tableware. (A) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed so that contamination of FOOD- and lip-contact surfaces is prevented.

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment:
4-204.112: In the back two door cooler, there was not an air thermometer to measure the air temperature of the unit. CORRECTED- The manager placed a thermometer in the unit. Ensure that all hot or refrigerated storage units have an air thermometer in them to accurately track the temperature of them. 

 (A) In refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure air temperature.

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.comment:
4-904.11: There are to-go containers on the counter in the breakfast area that are being stored with the food-contact surface exposed to contamination. Ensure that these containers have a cover placed over them to protect them from contamination or are inverted. Single service articles and utensils need to be stored in a manner that protect them from contamination

(A) cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed to prevent FOOD- and lip-contact surface contamination.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.12: The wall around the knives and magnetic knife strips is observed to be soiled with food splash. Ensure that this wall is cleaned and maintained cleaned to avoid contamination to the knives that are stored on the knife strips. Physical facilities should be cleaned as often as necessary to maintain them clean. 

(A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
Employee observed turning the faucet off without the use of a barrier after washing hands. CORRECTED- Provided education. Ensure employees use a paper towel to turn the faucet off after washing hands.
2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED. [P]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
No measurable sanitizer concentration observed at the dish machine. When the sanitize cycle began and the wheel turned to dispense sanitizer, it was dispensed onto the top of the machine as the hose was not connected to carry it into the dish compartment. Significant accumulation observed in this area of the dish machine indicates that this has been an ongoing problem. CORRECTED- MJ Kellner service rep was on site before the end of this inspection. Machine was repaired and observed dispensing at 50 ppm chlorine. 
-Clean the chemical accumulation from the top of the dish machine.
-Ensure staff monitor the sanitizer concentration and the tube connection.
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum concentration of 50-200ppm. [P]

findings.title: Food properly labeled; original container
findings.comment:
Unlabeled spray bottle observed under the microwave in the kitchen. CORRECTED- Employees indicated that the spray bottle contains oil for cooking. Spray bottle was labeled to indicate contents.
3-302.12: If in working container, FOOD not readily recognized or easily mistakable shall be identified with the common name of the FOOD. [C]

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
Wet wiping cloth observed on the kitchen counter near the coffee machine. Employee explained that it was used to wipe up coffee spills. Ensure wiping cloths for wiping up spills are maintained dry and used for no other purpose. After use, damp or wet cloths cannot be left on the countertop. CORRECTED- Cloth was removed and placed with dirty linens.
3-304.14: (A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. (D) Dry wiping cloths and sanitizing solution shall be free of FOOD debris and other soil. (E) Containers of sanitizing solution shall be stored off floor and used in manner to prevent contamination. (F) SINGLE-USE disposable sanitizer wipes shall be used in accordance with EPA labels. [C]

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment: 2-201.11: Observed facility to not have signed reporting agreements for all food employees. Provide signed employee reporting agreements for all food employees. (A) The PERMIT HOLDER shall require FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES to report to the PERSON IN CHARGE information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD. Report: Symptoms (all P except lesion), diagnosis (all P), and possible exposures (P).  (E) Responsibility of food employee to report symptoms/disease to PIC.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment: 4-602.12: Observed the interior of microwave in kitchen to be heavily soiled with food splash and debris. (A) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking and baking EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at least every 24 hours. This section does not apply to hot oil cooking and filtering EQUIPMENT if it is cleaned as specified in Subparagraph 4-602.11(D)(6). (B) The cavities and door seals of microwave ovens shall be cleaned at least every 24 hours by using the manufacturer's recommended cleaning procedure.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment: 4-303.11: Observed sanitizer solution available to not be testable using quaternary ammonia or chlorine test strips. New sanitizer bucket was made using chlorine bleach. New solution was tested at 200 ppm Cl-.(A) Cleaning agents used to clean EQUIPMENT shall be provided and available during all hours of operation. (B) Chemical SANITIZERS shall be provided and available during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment: 3-501.17: (A) Observed open gallons of milk in cooler to not have a date mark.  Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment: 6-501.16: Observed wet mop head to be stored head down in mop bucket.  After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to airdry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.
